messages:
alice: FYI support case from MacroPay — they're seeing a spike of 502/504s from the hosted inference API starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer says latencies jump and then errors. I can see tenant-level error rate increasing in Sentry.
ben: Thanks — can you paste the customer request pattern? Any auth/billing failures?
alice: Attaching excerpts. Looks like a high number of 401s from their SDK around the same time, followed by a flood of retries. Then our gateway queue depth climbs, continuous-batcher backlog rises and we hit the per-tenant queue depth limit -> timeouts.
carol: That sounds like the classic auth-retry amplification we've seen. If the client retries quickly on 401 it can saturate our ingress queues. Do we have traces for p95/p99 for the tenant?
david: Quick slices: link to dashboards (private). p95 jumped from 180ms to 1.4s; p99 to ~8s before the tail timeouts started returning 504s. Request queue depth metric shows spike from 200 -> 1400 in ~3 minutes and then lots of early-rejects. Logs show repeated token refresh failures: 
```
2026-03-17T10:11:58Z tenant=macropay req_id=abcd auth=401 "token_expired"
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z tenant=macropay req_id=abce retry=1
2026-03-17T10:12:04Z tenant=macropay req_id=abcf retry=2
2026-03-17T10:12:05Z tenant=macropay enqueue depth=312
2026-03-17T10:12:18Z tenant=macropay enqueue depth=1024 drop=true
2026-03-17T10:12:19Z gateway response=504 latency=30005ms
```
ben: Oof. So root cause = client token expiry + aggressive retry policy -> request storm -> queue saturation -> continuous-batcher backlog -> tail timeouts.
emma: Support confirmed MacroPay's billing system temporarily returned 402 for a few requests; their SDK treats 402/401 as retriable and blasts refresh attempts. They just rotated credentials but we still have in-flight flood.
carol: Immediate mitigations we can take: 1) Tenant rate-limit to cap ingress for macropay 2) Apply short-lived route to fallback to smaller model for that tenant to reduce per-request service time 3) Raise per-tenant enqueue limit temporarily (careful) 4) Ask customer to patch retry backoff. Which can we do right now?
ben: I'm oncall — I'll apply tenant ingress rate-limit and a fallback route. Don't raise global per-tenant limits — risk cross-tenant impact.
ben: Running: ```rbctl tenant set-throttle macropay --rps=20 --burst=40 --reason="auth-retry-storm 2026-03-17"```
incidents-bot: Action recorded: throttle applied to tenant macropay by ben at 2026-03-17T10:13:05Z
carol: Also enabling fallback route to small-gpt-v1 for macropay to cut token processing time: ```rbctl route add macropay --model=small-gpt-v1 --priority=low --timeout=20s```
david: Applied both. Queue depth dropped from 1024 -> 180 within 40s. Early-rejects reduced and 504 rate is falling.
alice: Customer confirm?
support-bot: Message from MacroPay: "Thanks, we've rotated tokens and see errors decreasing. Noticed big spike in retries — we'll deploy SDK fix with exponential backoff ASAP." :thumbsup:
emma: I'll keep monitoring for the next 30m and keep this thread updated. Also logging a postmortem item: add a rule to detect auth-related retry storms (401/402 bursts) and auto-apply tenant-level dampening in the future.
carol: Agreed — runbook update: add a checklist to check auth/billing status before scaling enqueue limits.
ben: Follow-up tasks: 1) ops to run cleanup to drain in-flight queue gracefully 2) platform to add heuristic for "auth-error amplified retry" 3) support to coordinate SDK patch with MacroPay. I'll open tickets.
emma: We're green for now — 504s are back to baseline and p95 trending down. Closing incident when stable for 30m.
alice: Thanks everyone. Saving logs and timeline to the ticket.
ben: Note for postmortem: possible improvement — circuit-breaker on per-tenant auth error rate that returns 429 to callers instead of allowing full enqueue.
carol: Agreed. Also consider exposing a customer-facing best-practice doc about retry backoffs for 4xx vs 5xx.
incidents-bot: Incident marked: mitigated at 2026-03-17T10:17:40Z"
